comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment:
I am currently an employee with Vasion located at 432 S Tech Ridge Drive, not far from Dixie Technical College. For employees to get to the Vasion building, there is a parking lot across the street (west) from Tech Ridge Parkway. Employees need to cross the street to get to work.

Within the last year, road work has been completed connecting Knowledge Way road, near Dixie Technical College, allowing students two ways to get to school, continuing southbound on Tech Ridge Parkway vs strictly taking Tech Ridge Drive.

I'm all for the city expanding and making traffic optimal. However, either students, staff, or whomever in between decide to constantly go down this road well past the posted 30 MPH speed limit. I've personally seen cars fly by as I try to make my way to the parking lot, thankful that I had not been there seconds prior because I certainly did not see them coming from down the hill to then.

I've discussed the issue with management on if any precautions can be taken, if any conversations have been had with the city, etc.. I am told that the *only* way the city will get involved, would be if there is an incident on this street. I do not think the city understands just how fast people fly through here. In fact, I'm positive the St. George Police Department could meet quota on this street alone just waiting a few hours up here.

One thought I've had would be simply making the intersection of Tech Ridge Drive and Tech Ridge Parkway a four way stop vs the current two way stop. This way people crossing the street can at least visibly see cars as they are forced to stop and wait for the four way traffic to go, and for those loosely obeying the law, at the very least force them to slow down. This intersection is outline in screenshots, and coordinates according to Google Maps is 37°06'06.0"N 113°35'37.4"W, so there is no confusion. There's no expectation of installing new street lights here, just two more simple stop signs could possibly save multiple lives.

There are public functions that happen here at the Vasion building, sometimes involving children. For example, upcoming holiday parties where family and friends are invited to the building. Is the city serious about someone potentially being struck here for anything to be done? For someone to potentially die here? Is there a budgetary reason why two more signs couldn't be installed here? Can someone from the city please explain why they do not care about safety on this street (come eat lunch near the school, there are cars and motorcycles revving engines and flying by both Tech Ridge Parkway & Drive)? Wouldn't installing signs be cheaper than potential lawsuits down the metaphorical road? Would it really take one of my nieces or nephews being struck by a car here for the city to do *anything*??

Thank you for your time.
